subject: Wave 0 runbook + ops questions for embed + rerank migration
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wang <alice@brightline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Wave 0 runbook + ops questions for embed + rerank migration

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. I put together a short "Wave 0" runbook so we can get alignment on the first production migration wave for Brightline search (attached: wave0-runbook-v1.pdf and seed_manifest.csv). High-level asks and proposed timeline below.

Key objectives for Wave 0:
- Validate rerank quality on a narrow segment (support articles + FAQ ~25k docs)
- Complete a backfill of recent content into the vector store (priming + unique id mapping)
- Run a canary (2% traffic) for 48 hours with automatic rollback on precision drop >5%

Immediate questions for your team:
1) Vector DB: Are you planning to use VectorStore Cloud (managed) or your self-hosted instance? If self-hosted, share the current index shard count and typical ingest TPS.
2) SLOs & acceptance: We suggested a canary threshold and rerank passthrough metrics in the runbook — are those acceptable or should we add business-specific checks?
3) Sample set: I've attached a small "rerank_eval_samples.jsonl" to illustrate the format we need for offline evals — can you confirm access and provide a handful of representative queries?

Proposed next steps (this week):
- Today: review runbook and answer Q1–Q3
- Thu: sync call (30m) to lock canary window and agree on evaluation queries
- Next Mon: start seed backfill (scope: new + updated docs from last 90 days)

Notes on attachments: seed_manifest.csv contains doc ids + timestamps; rerank_eval_samples.jsonl is a tiny sample (50 queries) for the eval team.

Thanks,

—Soojin Lee
Senior CSM, Onboarding
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: Alice Wang <alice@brightline.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightline Engineering <eng@brightline.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Wave 0 runbook + ops questions for embed + rerank migration

Soojin — thanks for the clear runbook. A couple quick answers and clarifications: 

1) Vector DB: we'll be using VectorStore self-hosted in our prod VPC (vstore-prod-03). Current shard count: 8. Average ingest TPS during working hours ~12 TPS, spikes to 35 TPS during batch loads.

2) Acceptance: the canary thresholds look reasonable — the product team wants to add a user-facing metric: click-through rate on search results (we'll give you a GA event id). If CTR drops >3% with a corresponding drop in precision, we want automatic rollback.

3) Sample set: confirmed, I can surface 200 query samples by tomorrow afternoon. We will also export an initial set of 1,000 negative examples for rerank calibration.

One operational question: will Redwood's backfill agent do live re-ingestion (POST) or can we push a snapshot + bulk ingest? We prefer bulk ingest to avoid overwhelming the index.

I'll also loop in our procurement lead separately about SOW/DocuSign.

—Alice
Head of Search Product
Brightline
alice@brightline.com

Thanks Alice — good notes. Short answers inline then a couple operational constraints: 

- Vector DB bulk vs live: we recommend a bulk snapshot + bulk ingest for Wave 0 (less risk). Redwood's backfill agent supports both; for bulk we'll provide an S3 manifest + ordering token so you can control ingestion concurrency.

- Canary metric: adding CTR makes sense. We'll include an event ingestion check and a CTR delta rule in the canary policy. Implementation detail: if CTR telemetry isn't available in the first 48 hours, the canary will fall back to precision@10 and answer latency.

- Shard count note: with 8 shards we should be conservative on batch size. I'll add an operational throttle and suggested concurrency (3 writers) to the runbook.

Attachments and links:
- rerank_eval_samples.jsonl (attached): format includes query, gold doc ids, and a short business label. Please scrub any PII before sending full samples.
- Runbook link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-wave0-docs

Proposed call time: Thu 08/21 10:00am PT (30m). If that works, we'll send calendar invite.

—Soojin
Senior CSM, Onboarding
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Wang <alice@brightline.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Wave 0 runbook + ops questions for embed + rerank migration

Looping in a couple ops notes from the implementation side: 

- Canary window: we can do 48 hours over a Thursday–Friday window to observe both weekday and after-hours behavior. Suggest starting Thu 09/04 00:00 PT to capture production search volume.
- Acceptance criteria (draft): precision@10 drop <= 5%; CTR delta <= 3% (as Alice requested); 95th pct latency increase <= 120ms. Any automatic rollback will be triggered only if two of the three metrics breach simultaneously.
- Eval plan: we'll run an offline rerank sweep using your 1,000 negative examples + our holdout; will push results to the shared Drive folder and tag runs with run_id.

Operational tasks assigned: 
- Ben: prepare the S3 manifest + ingestion token for bulk backfill. (Ben: aim for a dry-run by Mon 08/25).
- Logan: coordinate the canary traffic routing and implement the CTR fallback rule in the tracing hooks.
- Camila: finalize the eval sampling script and upload to Drive.

Marissa
Implementation Lead, Redwood Dedicated
